ai.description: Bronchocela danieli is a slender lizard reaching 12 cm in snout-vent length. It is bright green with a distinct, elongated, black-tipped nuchal crest and a prominent black spot behind each eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Bronchocela danieli* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged white stripe running along the side of its head and neck, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Bronchocela danieli* inhabits the evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found in moist, dense vegetation at mid-to-high altitudes.
ai.behavior: Daniel's Forest Lizard is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects and invertebrates among the foliage and tree trunks during daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Bronchocela danieli* is oviparous, laying clutches of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Bronchocela danieli* is endemic to the Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal, where it inhabits tropical forest environments at low elevations.
